content.user_title: Roleplay a Tense Alien Storm Survival Story
content.value_statement: Writers and players who want a ready-made, high-tension interactive fiction chapter often lack a structured script with pacing, choices, and branches. This skill provides a complete storm-survival roleplay where you guide Stella Chen through priority decisions, dramatic setbacks, and mysterious discoveries on an alien planet.
actual_capabilities: Runs a five-phase storm-survival roleplay: warning, storm arrival, storm eye, second half, and aftermath.
Presents timed priority decisions such as securing shelter, supplies, water, and communications.
Delivers three distinct story endings: heroic survival, heavy losses, and mysterious discovery.
Maintains a consistent character voice for Stella Chen, mixing Chinese and English dialogue.
Sets up follow-on chapters like alien encounter and signal-tower rebuilding through story hooks.
limitations: Contains only narrative content and does not execute code or perform any system actions.
Dialogue is bilingual Chinese and English, which may not suit purely English-speaking audiences.
The storyline is fixed to one scenario and does not adapt to arbitrary settings or genres.
It depends on prior chapters for full character and world context.

use_cases.title: Guided Solo Roleplay Session
use_cases.description: A player runs the chapter with an AI assistant to experience a tense, choice-driven survival story on an alien planet.

use_cases.title: Writing Reference for Narrative Designers
use_cases.description: A writer studies the phase structure, pacing, and branching endings as a template for building their own tension-driven story chapters.

use_cases.title: Language Learning Through Story
use_cases.description: A learner reads the mixed Chinese-English dialogue to practice both languages within an engaging survival narrative.

prompt_templates.title: Start the Storm Chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Begin the Surviving the Storm chapter. Play as Stella Chen and start with the storm warning phase.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Priority Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: During the preparation phase, I want to prioritize securing communications first. Continue the story based on that choice.
prompt_templates.scenario: Responding to a timed decision point

prompt_templates.title: Explore the Storm Eye Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: When the storm eye arrives, have Stella go outside to assess camp damage, then continue the narrative.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choosing branch B during the storm eye

prompt_templates.title: Reach the Mysterious Discovery Ending
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide the story toward the mysterious discovery ending, revealing evidence of intelligent life, and set up the next chapter.
prompt_templates.scenario: Steering toward a specific ending and continuation

output_examples.input: Begin the Surviving the Storm chapter and start with the warning phase.
output_examples.output: Stella reacts to her scanner detecting a category-5 storm. She lists her priorities aloud, then asks the player which task matters most in the limited two-hour window before the storm hits.

output_examples.input: I want to prioritize securing communications first.
output_examples.output: Stella acknowledges the choice, protects the communicator and scanner in waterproof bags, and moves supplies to the inner shelter as the first strong gusts begin.

output_examples.input: Have Stella go outside during the storm eye to assess damage.
output_examples.output: Stella steps out into the calm eye, describes the devastation to her camp, notices scattered crystals and unfamiliar footprints, then sprints back as the storm wall returns.

best_practices: Respond to each decision point with a clear priority so the story can branch meaningfully.
Stay in character and reply to Stella's questions as if you are her remote contact.
Let the pacing build tension by following the five phases in order rather than skipping ahead.
anti_patterns: Treating the fenced dialogue blocks as executable commands; they are only story formatting.
Trying to break the fixed scenario into an unrelated genre, which loses the intended tension.
Rushing to an ending without engaging the timed decisions, which flattens the narrative payoff.

faq.question: Does this skill run any code or shell commands?
faq.answer: No. It contains only narrative Markdown. The triple backticks in the file are formatting for dialogue blocks and execute nothing.

faq.question: What language is the story written in?
faq.answer: The dialogue mixes Chinese and English, with narration and character speech blending both languages.

faq.question: Do I need to play earlier chapters first?
faq.answer: It helps. The chapter references a prior crash and an established camp, so playing earlier chapters gives fuller context, though you can still enjoy it standalone.

faq.question: How long does the chapter take?
faq.answer: The author estimates 30 to 40 minutes for a full playthrough with a high tension level.

faq.question: Are there multiple endings?
faq.answer: Yes. There are three branches: heroic survival, heavy losses, and a mysterious discovery that hints at intelligent alien life.

faq.question: What chapters follow this one?
faq.answer: Recommended follow-ups include the alien encounter chapter, the signal-tower rebuild, a daily-science study of storm crystals, and exploring exposed ancient ruins.
